The function $f(x)$ is defined on $(-\infty ,\infty ).$
The graph of the second derivative $y={f}^{″}(x)$ of the function $f(x)$ intersects the $x$-axis at the points $x=-2$ and $x=3,$ as shown above. Find the interval on which the function $f(x)$ is concave down.

feedback.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is concave down over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${f}^{″}(x)<0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

From the plotted graph of $y={f}^{″}(x)$, we can  see that ${f}^{″}(x)<0$ on the interval   $(-2,3)$ 

Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is concave down on the interval $(\,-2,3\,).$
